<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="PARTI"><!--Anchor--></a>PART I</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="ITEM1BUSINESS"><!--Anchor--></a>ITEM 1&#8212;BUSINESS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">GENERAL</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Official Payments is a leading provider of electronic payment solutions for over 3,000 Clients across all 50 states, Puerto Rico and the District of Columbia. During the past year more than 12 million Customers and Constituents of our Clients utilized our services. &#160;Official Payments' solutions enable government agencies, educational institutions, utility companies and charitable organizations to accept payments by credit card, debit card and electronic check via mobile devices, the Internet, telephone and point of sale devices.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Utilizing our payment solutions, Clients can reduce, if not eliminate, the costs of accepting payments from their Customers. &#160;Additionally, Clients can comply with Payment Card Industry (PCI) data security requirements and other payment industry standards while offering their Customers a secure and convenient means of payment. The demand for our services has been driven by an increasing willingness, and preference, of consumers to utilize electronic payments. Consumers appreciate the flexibility, speed, convenience, security, tracking and verifiability of electronic payments as well as the variety of funding sources our solutions allow them to use to make payments. Merchants and billers have been expanding their use of electronic payments in response to consumer demand, in an effort to lower their costs to manage and deliver payment functionality to comply with regulatory mandates.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our business consists of two reportable segments: Payment Solutions and our Voice and Systems Automation (VSA) business. We are in the process of winding-down the VSA business and expect to complete this effort in fiscal 2014. In the interim we are not pursuing new VSA clients but continue to support existing contracts.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Revenues from our Payment Solutions operations were $134.4&#160;million for fiscal 2012. Fiscal 2012 transaction volume decreased 0.5% and total dollars processed increased 10.1% over fiscal 2011. &#160;Revenues from our Payment Solutions operations make up 99.0% of our revenues from Continuing Operations.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 6pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We generally provide our payment solutions to a core set of Client types including:</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Norcross, GA. &#160;As of September&#160;30, 2012, we had 237 employees and 45 contractors.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">PAYMENT SOLUTIONS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our core business consists of Payment Solutions that we offer to a variety of federal, state and local governments, higher education institutions, utility companies, and charitable organizations. Our Clients utilize our services to provide electronic payment alternatives to their Customers or Constituents. Examples of payments made utilizing our services include federal and state income taxes, real property taxes, &#160;court and other fines, tuition, utility bills, and charitable donations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 9pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">2</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both">
<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Back to table of contents<br>
</a></div>
</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both">&#160;</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both">We offer our Clients two primary pricing options: convenience fees paid by the Customer, and Client absorbed fees paid by the Client. These fees are generally calculated as a percentage of the underlying transaction amount, but may also be expressed as a fixed fee in some cases. Our Clients include the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), 27 state governments, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, and over 3,000 additional Clients. Across all of our Clients, we processed approximately 20 million transactions, representing $9.0 billion in payments during fiscal 2012.</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Payment Solutions revenue and transaction volumes have increased over the past nine years. &#160;These increases are attributable to several factors:</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(1) increased adoption of electronic payment options among billers;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(2) general market shift in consumer preference from cash and check to electronic forms of payment; and</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(3) expansion of our Client base into new types, including charitable giving.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">STRATEGIC REVIEW AND REFOCUS OF BUSINESS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the fall of 2006 our board of directors oversaw a strategic review of our business that resulted in a decision to focus our efforts on growing Payment Solutions and divesting other non-related businesses. During fiscal 2009, we completed the divestiture of our Government Business Process Outsourcing (GBPO) and our Packaged Software Systems Integrations (PSSI) businesses. At the same time, we invested in diversifying our base of Payment Solutions Clients, especially in the higher education and utility markets. Reflecting the progress of this initiative, the revenue contributed by our federal income tax business has decreased from 32% in fiscal 2006 to 19% of Payment Solutions revenue in fiscal 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following chart shows the change in revenue contribution from each primary Client type for the past three years:</div>

<div>DATA SECURITY</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The integrity and security of Client and Customer data is a priority for Official Payments. We are compliant with leading security industry standards required to process electronic payments; including the Payment Card Industry (PCI) Data Security Standard and the requirements of the National Automated Clearing House Association (NACHA). We perform periodic reviews of our systems and processes to ensure compliance with industry security standards and also undergo an annual audit of our security standards by the IRS.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal 2011, we expanded the responsibilities of the Data Security Committee of our Board of Directors to include the review and assessment of operational risks, and the Committee was renamed the Data Security and Operational Risk Committee. &#160;The committee's primary function is to act on behalf of the Board in the oversight of data security management and operational risk assessment responsibilities as defined by applicable law and regulations, and to monitor compliance with policies and procedures developed by Official Payments management. &#160;The Data Security and Operational Risk Committee oversees the Company's work on identifying and evaluating security and related operational risks, on implementing safeguards and programs to address data security, and on the mitigation of systems, operational and security risks. &#160;The committee works with our management team to enhance current technical policies and procedures. develop new technical policies and procedures to strengthen security and operational safeguards, and ensure that the company has adequate insurance to protect it from risk exposure.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">TECHNOLOGY</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a result of acquisitions since 2002, we operate our business on three different technology platforms. In 2009, we decided to consolidate our operations onto a single technology platform over time. &#160;Subsequently, we recognized that our systems required a company-wide infrastructure upgrade prior to the platform consolidation. Thus, during fiscal 2011 and fiscal 2012 we performed an $8.3 million infrastructure upgrade, bringing our systems to a state where the platform consolidation may begin. &#160;We expect to complete the consolidation by the end of December 2013. We believe this consolidation will result in significant operating efficiencies and will enable us to develop and incorporate new features and functionality into our core product set.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SALES AND MARKETING</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our Payment Solutions sales and marketing objective is to develop lasting relationships with new and existing Customers and Clients that result in repeat business, cross-sale opportunities, and the development of our Payment Solutions business.&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">To expand and enhance Customer adoption and utilization of our solutions, we are launching enhanced functionality for our <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MyAccount</font> payment solution.&#160; <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MyAccount</font> is a personal registration function that enables Customers to manage their online bills and payment methods for a range of Client billers, all from a single internet site.&#160; We also plan to launch new e-commerce products and payment services including additional payment channels such as mobile and walk-up payments beginning in fiscal 2013.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition we employ an integrated marketing strategy that seeks to create broad-scale awareness of our solutions, while also supporting targeted marketing initiatives.&#160; Historically, these efforts have been delivered through the resources and communication channels of our co-marketing relationships, our Clients and our own Official Payments communication channels.&#160; Our use of co-marketing relationships has steadily diminished as the Official Payments Customer base and our Client footprint have grown, and as we have successfully developed our own online targeted communication channels including email, mobile marketing, web promotion and cross sale initiatives.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For Clients, we have sharpened our sales and relationship management focus by creating a Large Client Management Team distinct from our Field Sales Team that is now solely responsible for acquiring new Clients.&#160; The Large Client Management Team is comprised of experienced relationship managers who work in </div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS</div>

We rely on a combination of confidentiality, licensing and other contractual arrangements, as well as trade secret, copyright and trademark laws to protect our proprietary rights and the proprietary rights of third parties from whom we license intellectual property. &#160;We also enter into nondisclosure agreements with our employees, vendors, subcontractors, and consultants, and we control distribution of our proprietary information and trade secrets.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Official Payments has provided electronic payment solutions since 1996 and currently provides solutions for over 3,000 Clients across all 50 states, Puerto Rico and the District of Columbia.&#160; We believe we compete favorably based on the competitive factors outlined above and face significant competition in our key markets from large global companies who leverage a broader breadth of business lines related to payment processing, and who have greater resources.&#160; We also face competition from smaller competitors who have established reputations and relationships with Clients and partners in certain regions.&#160; Examples of companies that currently or potentially could compete with us include Link2Gov Corp., a subsidiary of FIS; WorldPay; CheckFree and Bill Matrix, subsidiaries of Fiserv; SallieMae Business Office Solutions; TouchNet Information Systems, Inc; Oracle Corporation; Point &amp; Pay; Online Resources and NiC, Inc.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">GOVERNMENT REGULATIONS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 1, 2011, the Durbin Amendment provisions of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010 (Financial Reform Act) became effective. The Durbin Amendment limits debit card discount fees charged by card issuing banks. As a result of the Durbin Amendment, beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2012, we experienced a decrease in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Direct Costs</font> in our Consolidated Statements of Operations. The decrease reflected the impact of the Durbin Amendment on the debit card transactions that we process. We continue to experience the benefit of the Durbin Amendment on debit card discount fees in fiscal 2013. We are unable to predict the long-term consequences of the Durbin Amendment on the debit and credit card markets and related processing fees.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Additionally, our business is subject to numerous federal, state and local laws and regulations as a money services business, as a licensed money transmitter, and under anti-money laundering laws including under the USA Patriot Act and regulations administered by the U.S Department of Treasury.&#160; We are licensed as a </div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SEASONALITY OF BUSINESS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our business experiences seasonal fluctuations in payment volumes driven by due dates of taxes, tuition and other obligations. This seasonality causes corresponding fluctuations in our revenues and direct costs. Our general and administrative, and selling and marketing expenses are less seasonal in nature. These factors cause variability in our quarterly results. For example, our payment volumes are typically higher in our fiscal third quarter ending June 30<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">th</sup> due to the U.S. federal income tax season and are typically lower in our fiscal fourth quarter.

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. &#160;You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below in addition to the other information included or incorporated by reference in this Form 10-K, before making an investment decision with respect to our common stock. &#160;If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition or results of operations could be materially and adversely affected and you may lose all or part of your investment.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following factors and other risks could cause our actual results to differ materially from those contained in forward-looking statements in this Form 10-K.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 9pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We operate in a highly competitive market and may not be able to compete successfully. &#160;</font>The electronic payment transaction market is intensely competitive and rapidly evolving. &#160;We compete against numerous international, national and local firms, including banks, other financial institutions, and multi-national payment providers, many of which have significantly greater resources than we do. &#160;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">These competitors may devote greater resources to product development, technology systems, marketing, and sales allowing them to leverage their financial assets, customer base, political relationships, and name recognition. They may also have greater liquidity and lower cost structures enabling them to offer more aggressive pricing and secure better terms from vendors.</font> &#160;Some competitors are able to undercut our prices and operate at significant losses for extended periods of time. &#160;We expect c<font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ompetition to intensify as established and emerging companies enter into business combinations and expand into our market. &#160;In addition, evolving and enhanced technologies, including new payment acceptance methods and applications, may increase competition and reduce our market share. </font>If we do not compete successfully, any one of these factors could have a material adverse effect on our operating results and financial condition.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our business is dependent on the efficient and effective operation of our technology systems and platforms. &#160;</font>We operate on multiple technology platforms and a complex technology infrastructure including sophisticated hardware and software. &#160;We currently maintain three payment processing platforms in: San Jose, California; Norcross, Georgia; and Tulsa, Oklahoma. &#160;Our operations, systems and platforms could be disrupted or fail to perform properly for many reasons including operational or technical failures, human error, failure of third-party support or services, system failure due to age and lack of integrity of hardware and software infrastructure, existence of single points of failure, or diminished availability of our services causing us to fail to meet contractual service level requirements. &#160;Our operations, systems and platforms may also be disrupted or fail due to catastrophic events such as natural disasters, telecommunications failures, power outages, cyber-attacks, war, terrorist attacks, or other events beyond our control. &#160;In fiscal 2012 we completed a multi-million dollar project to upgrade and replace significant portions of our infrastructure including the majority of our servers, system equipment, and software. &#160;Despite these efforts, w<font style="BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">e experience occasional system interruptions and outages that make our services unavailable or slow to respond. <div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="ITEM2PROPERTIES"><!--Anchor--></a>ITEM 2&#8212;PROPERTIES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of September&#160;30, 2012, we leased or subleased 55,719 square feet of space in various locations in the United States. &#160;This includes 29,161&#160;square feet of space in Georgia, California and Oklahoma, to support our Payment Solutions operations, as well as 25,583 square feet in Reston, Virginia (our former corporate headquarters), which we sublet following the relocation of our corporate headquarters to Norcross, Georgia. &#160;In addition, we own a 28,060&#160;square-foot building in Alabama that houses certain administrative, call center, and other operations staff.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Payment Solutions net revenue and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations are supplemental non-GAAP financial measures. GAAP means generally accepted accounting principles in the United States. We define Payment Solutions net revenue as Payment Solutions gross revenue less Discount fees, which includes interchange fees and other processing-related dues, assessments and fees. Payment Solutions gross revenue is defined as revenue from continuing operations less non-Payment Solutions revenue. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations is equal to net income from continuing operations plus (a) interest income (expense) and other income(expense), net; (b) provision or benefit for income taxes; (c) depreciation and amortization; (d) share based compensation expense; (e) gain or loss on sale of investments; and (f) restructuring charges. For a description of our use of Payment Solutions<font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>net revenue and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations and a reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to their most comparable GAAP measures, see the discussion and related tables below<font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We believe non-GAAP financial measures, such as Payment Solutions net revenue and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations are useful to an investor in evaluating our performance for the following reasons:</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="ITEM7MANAGEMENTSDISCUSSIO"><!--Anchor--></a>ITEM 7&#8212;MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations includes forward-looking statements. &#160;We have based these forward-looking statements on our current plans, expectations and beliefs about future events. &#160;Our actual performance could differ materially from the expectations and beliefs reflected in the forward-looking statements in this section and throughout this report, as a result of the risks, uncertainties and assumptions discussed under Item 1A&#8212;Risk Factors of this Annual Report on Form 10-K and other factors discussed in this section. &#160;For information regarding what constitutes a forward-looking statement please refer to the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act Safe Harbor Statement on page&#160;.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">OVERVIEW</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Official Payments provides electronic payment solutions for over 3,000 Clients across all 50 states, Puerto Rico and the District of Columbia. &#160;Official Payments' solutions enable government agencies, educational institutions, utility companies and charitable organizations to accept payments by credit card, debit card and electronic check via mobile, web, telephone and point of sale environments.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">KEY FISCAL 2012 INITIATIVES AND EVENTS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal 2012 Official Payments continued to focus on initiatives aimed at improving the quality and reliability of our technology infrastructure, and on improving our operational efficiency.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During our first fiscal quarter, we completed the relocation of our principal executive offices to Norcross, Georgia from Reston, Virginia. As previously disclosed, we believe that our operating and personnel costs will be lower in Georgia than in Virginia and that Georgia offers a labor force with more experience in electronic payments.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal 2012, we completed substantial upgrades to our hardware, software, and services infrastructure to improve the reliability and security of our core payments systems, and to provide network capacity that will enable us to deliver expanded product capabilities and handle future increases in transaction volumes. As of September 30, 2012, we completed this project and the related assets were placed into service.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We consolidated certain operations functions, which allowed us to reduce our number of active data centers from five to three as of the end of fiscal 2012 thus reducing related costs and operational complexity.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective with the commencement of fiscal 2012, the Durbin Amendment to the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010 became effective. The Durbin Amendment limits debit card discount fees charged by card issuing banks. Because we process a large number of debit card transactions, the Durbin Amendment has caused us to experience a meaningful decrease in Direct Costs in our Consolidated Statements of Operations throughout fiscal 2012 and to date in fiscal 2013. Given that this cost savings is a function of regulatory action, we are unable to predict the long-term impact of the Durbin Amendment.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">KEY FISCAL 2013 INITIATIVES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Platform Consolidation</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We currently support three processing platforms, a legacy of past acquisitions. We believe that our Clients would be better served by combining our payment operations into a single processing platform. By using one platform we believe that we will be more efficient, more flexible in delivering new product features and services, and able to provide a better overall Client and Customer experience. We therefore intend to execute the previously discussed platform consolidation project with a target of being substantially complete by the end of calendar 2013. We estimate that this consolidation project will cost approximately $2.5 million, a substantial cost savings, compared to prior estimates.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; FONT-SIZE: 9pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">17</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Back to table of contents<br>
</a></div>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Product</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Building products that Customers want to use is important to our ability to sign up new Clients and to get their Customers and Constituents to make more payments utilizing Official Payments' services. We intend to supplement our current browser-based mobile solutions with the launch of native applications (apps) for iPad, iPhone, and Android users in fiscal 2013. In addition, we believe that there is a significant opportunity to enable our Clients to deliver&#160;their bills electronically to their Customers and Constituents, so we plan to introduce a suite of electronic bill presentment solutions in fiscal 2013 as well.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Continued Operational Efficiency</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We also continue to work to reduce our overall processing costs, including discount fees and other related transaction processing fees. We believe that promoting lower cost, higher margin payment types may result in both higher Customer adoption and higher Payment Solutions net revenue.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">RESULTS OF OPERATIONS&#8212;FISCAL 2012 AND 2011</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The increase in Payment Solutions net revenue in fiscal 2012 was driven primarily by lower discount fees we incurred in connection with processing payments. &#160;These better rates are primarily a function of cost benefits we realized as result of the Durbin Amendment and savings associated with negotiating lower processing fees. There is no assurance that these savings will continue in future periods.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Payment Solutions Revenues:</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> &#160;</font>Our core business consists of Payment Solutions that we offer to a variety of federal, state and local governments, utility companies, higher education institutions, and charitable organizations. Our Clients utilize our services to provide electronic payment alternatives to their Customers or Constituents. Examples of payment transactions made utilizing our services include federal and state income taxes, real property taxes, tuition payments, court and other fines, utility and other payment obligations and charitable donations. &#160;In fiscal 2012 we processed approximately 20 million transactions, representing approximately $9.0 billion in payment volume.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We offer our Clients two primary pricing options: convenience fees paid by the Customer, and absorbed fees paid by the Client. These fees are generally calculated as a percentage of the underlying transaction amount, but may also be expressed as a fixed fee in some cases. &#160;Payment Solutions revenue is comprised almost solely of such fees.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal 2012, we processed 0.5% fewer transactions than in fiscal 2011, principally due to a decrease in transaction volume in our utilities market. &#160;The decline in transaction volume was more than offset by a 10.6% increase in our average payment size, which resulted in a 10.1% increase in total dollars processed in fiscal 2012 over fiscal 2011. &#160;Most of the growth in payment size and dollars processed was attributable to higher education, federal, state and local government Clients. &#160;Offsetting these increases, we experienced a 15.0% decrease in transactions for utilities Clients during fiscal year 2012 versus fiscal year 2011, due to a decrease in transactions for large utilities.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our gross margin from Continuing Operations is calculated by subtracting (i) direct costs from Continuing Operations from (ii) revenue from Continuing Operations. Our gross margin percentage is calculated by dividing (i) gross margin from Continuing Operations by (ii) revenue from Continuing Operations. Our gross margin and gross margin percentage depend on four principal factors: revenue, cost, the number of transactions processed, and the mix of transactions by Client type and payment type.</div>

<div>
<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 36pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#183;</div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: auto; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our revenue from a transaction depends on whether we receive a flat fee or a fee based on a percentage of the transaction amount. &#160;The type and amount of a fee depends on many competitive considerations, including regulations of payment networks, industry competition, and the level of service that we provide at each Client. If our revenue is equal to a percentage of the amount paid, then revenue will also be affected by all the factors that cause payment amounts to vary.</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div>
<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 36pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#183;</div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: auto; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our direct cost for a transaction depends principally on how the payment is made. It costs us more to process certain types of transactions such as credit card payments and less to process other types of transactions such as electronic checks and debit card payments. &#160;We discuss our direct costs in more detail below.</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

</td>
<td style="WIDTH: auto; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The number of transactions we process and the mix of transactions among Client types are influenced by, among other things: Customers' and Constituents' payment preferences; the type of payments being processed (annual, monthly, quarterly, or periodic); the market penetration of electronic payment options among federal, state, and local governments, higher education institutions, utility companies and charitable organizations; the success of our sales and marketing efforts; and the usability of our products and services.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Each of these factors is subject to change, and as a result, our gross margin from Continuing Operations and our gross margin percentage may change at different rates.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We expect to experience continued growth in revenue, Payment Solutions net revenue and gross margin in fiscal 2013 as compared with fiscal 2012, as we execute on our key strategic initiatives.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">VSA Revenues:</font> &#160;Consistent with our plan to wind down our VSA operation, our revenue decreased for fiscal 2012 when compared to fiscal 2011, as underlying contracts expire. &#160;We expect to see continued revenue decreases during fiscal 2013 and 2014.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Direct Costs (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Direct costs, which represent costs directly attributable to providing services to Clients, consist predominantly of discount fees. &#160;Discount fees include payment card interchange fees, assessments payable to banks and payment card processing fees. &#160;Other, less significant costs include: payroll and payroll-related costs; travel-related expenditures; co-location and telephony costs; and the cost of hardware, software and equipment sold to VSA Clients. &#160;The following table provides a year-over-year comparison of direct costs incurred by our Continuing Operations during fiscal years 2012 and 2011:</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following sections discuss the key factors that caused these changes in direct costs for Continuing Operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Payment Solutions Direct Costs:</font> &#160;Discount fees decreased $6.5&#160;million, or 6.8%, from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012. The decrease in discount fees is a result of cost savings from the Durbin Amendment, as well as lower negotiated processing fees for some of our Clients.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other direct costs increased $0.6 million, or 10.1%, during fiscal 2012 as compared with fiscal 2011 as a result of increased co-location facility costs.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>VSA Direct Costs:</u></font> &#160;During fiscal 2012, direct costs from our VSA operations increased $0.4 million, or 156.6%, as compared with fiscal 2011. &#160;This increase is attributable to the costs associated with contracted services provided in connection with a one-time project for a VSA Client. &#160;As we continue the wind down of VSA, we expect VSA direct costs to decrease during fiscal 2013.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>General and Administrative (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General and administrative (G&amp;A) expenses consist primarily of: payroll and payroll-related costs for technology, product management, finance, accounting, legal and executive management; information systems; and outside services fees, including regulatory compliance, audits and other costs that we incur as a public company. Information systems expenses include costs to enhance our processing platforms as well</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Payment Solutions General and Administrative:</u></font> &#160;During fiscal 2012, Payment Solutions G&amp;A expenses increased $7.5 million, or 33.0%, over fiscal year 2011. Several factors contributed to the overall increase in G&amp;A expenses during fiscal 2012. &#160;First, we accrued performance-related compensation expenses $3.3 million higher than in fiscal 2011. &#160;Second, our share based compensation expense is $1.8 million greater in fiscal 2012 than in fiscal 2011 primarily due to the fiscal 2011 reversal of $1.5 million of expense related to restricted stock units ("RSUs") that had been granted to our former CEO. &#160;The vesting conditions of the RSUs were not satisfied and $1.5 million of previously recorded expense was reversed in the quarter ended March 31, 2011. Third, during fiscal 2012, we recorded a restructuring charge of $1.6 million, including relocation costs of $0.1 million, related to the relocation of our principal executive offices from Reston, Virginia to Norcross, Georgia. &#160;In connection with vacating and subletting our Reston, Virginia facility we wrote off certain balances associated with our original lease agreement including leasehold improvements, net of accumulated amortization and deferred rent. Lastly, we incurred an increase in nonperformance-related employee compensation expense of $1.2 million in fiscal 2012 as compared to fiscal 2011, primarily as a result of increased headcount in our technology organization, related to the previously discussed infrastructure and platform consolidation projects.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We expect fiscal 2013 G&amp;A expenses to decrease over fiscal 2012, due to the one-time nature of our restructuring costs, as well as an expected decrease in management incentive plan costs.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>VSA General and Administrative:</u></font> &#160;G&amp;A costs for VSA operations increased $0.2&#160;million in fiscal 2012 over fiscal 2011. &#160;We expect to see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">de minimis</font> general and administrative expenses for our VSA operation during fiscal 2013, as we continue to wind-down the related contracts.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Selling and Marketing (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Selling and marketing expenses consist primarily of payroll and payroll-related costs for sales, large account management and marketing personnel, sales commissions, advertising and marketing expenditures and travel-related expenditures. &#160;We expect selling and marketing expenses to fluctuate from quarter to quarter due to a variety of factors, such as increased advertising and marketing expenses incurred in connection with the April 15th federal income tax payment deadline. &#160;The following table provides a year-over-year comparison of selling and marketing costs incurred during fiscal 2012 and 2011:</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Depreciation expense was $0.6 million higher in fiscal 2012 as compared with fiscal 2011, due to internally developed software and infrastructure assets, being placed into service during fiscal 2012. This amount was almost completely offset by a decrease in amortization expense due to certain intangible assets becoming fully amortized. &#160;We did not incur depreciation or amortization expense for our VSA operation during fiscal 2012 or 2011. &#160;We expect fiscal 2013 depreciation and amortization expense to be consistent with the level in fiscal 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Other Income (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Interest income (expense), net: </u></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>Interest income during fiscal 2012 decreased $0.08&#160;million compared to fiscal 2011 primarily due to a decrease in interest rates earned on our invested cash. &#160;Our interest rates fluctuate with changes in the marketplace.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Income Tax Provision (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our income tax provision from continuing operations was $54,000 in fiscal 2012, a $9,000 increase over fiscal 2011. The provision for income taxes represents state tax obligations incurred by our Payment Solutions operations and an intra-period tax allocation between continuing and discontinued operations. &#160;Our Consolidated Statements of Operations for fiscal 2012 and 2011 do not reflect a federal tax provision because of offsetting adjustments to our deferred tax asset valuation allowance, which reduces any tax benefit to zero. &#160;Our effective tax rates differ from the federal statutory rate due to state income taxes, tax-exempt interest income and the charge for establishing a valuation allowance on our net deferred tax assets. &#160;Our future tax rate may vary due to factors including, but not limited to: the relative income contribution by tax jurisdiction; changes in statutory tax rates; the amount of tax exempt interest income generated during the year; changes in our valuation allowance; our ability to utilize net operating losses and any non-deductible items related to acquisitions or other nonrecurring charges.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Tax Loss Carryforwards</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At September&#160;30, 2012, we had $125.7&#160;million of federal net operating loss carryforwards, which expire beginning in fiscal 2018 through 2032, and $109.0&#160;million of state net operating loss carryforwards, most of which begin to expire after fiscal 2018 through 2032. &#160;Of the $125.7&#160;million of federal net operating loss carryforward and $109.0&#160;million of state net operating loss carryforwards, $48.6&#160;million and $28.1&#160;million, respectively, were acquired with the purchase of Official Payments Corporation in 2002.&#160; As of September&#160;30, 2012 approximately $108.3&#160;million of our federal net operating loss carryforwards do not have any restrictions.&#160; Our acquired federal net operating loss carryforward is limited to $3.4 million per year pursuant to Internal Revenue Code Section 382, and approximately $11.2&#160;million is still limited to this annual amount.&#160; If future ownership changes occur, there could be further limitations to our federal net operating loss carryforwards.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Payment Solutions Revenues:</font> &#160;During fiscal 2011, we processed 7.3% more transactions than in fiscal 2010, representing 5.7% more dollars processed. &#160;The lower growth in dollars processed, as compared with growth in transactions, was due primarily to an increase in transactions from Customers with lower average dollar size per transaction. Furthermore, the economic environment also caused the average payment size to decline. &#160;The combination of increased transactions processed, with lower average payment size resulted in minimal revenue growth in fiscal 2011.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Additionally, we experienced an 11.8% decrease in transactions processed for utility Clients, versus the previous year, primarily because many of the large utilities that became Official Payments Clients when ChoicePay was acquired did not renew their contracts. &#160;The majority of other Client types experienced increases in transactions processed, ranging from 8.1% to 18.0% during fiscal 2011 as compared to fiscal 2010.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">VSA Revenues:</font> &#160;Consistent with the plan to wind down our VSA operation, revenue decreased for fiscal 2011 when compared to fiscal 2010, as a result of contract completions.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Direct Costs (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Payment Solutions Direct Costs:</font> &#160;A 7.3% increase in transaction volume during fiscal 2011 was the primary cause of the 4.5% increase in discount fees over fiscal 2010. &#160;Further contributing to the increase in discount fees were the fluctuation in payment methods used by Customers as well as an increase in discount fees charged by one of the payment networks. &#160;In addition, during fiscal 2010 we recognized a one-time reduction in cost of $0.3&#160;million from settlement funds received related to payment card processing fees.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The decrease in other direct costs was primarily attributable to a $0.3&#160;million decrease in telephony costs as a result of our efforts to improve efficiencies in our telephony structure. &#160;We also benefited from a $0.1&#160;million decrease in labor and labor-related expenses, which includes temporary labor, primarily due to efforts to more efficiently staff our customer service department during the income tax season. &#160;In addition, we benefited from $0.2&#160;million in reduced non-capitalized equipment purchases, software maintenance and other miscellaneous costs. &#160;Offsetting these decreases was $0.1&#160;million in one-time expense associated with integration costs for certain higher education Clients.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>VSA Direct Costs:</u></font> &#160;Product and material costs decreased $0.5&#160;million during fiscal 2011 compared to fiscal 2010. &#160;The completion of several projects meant that certain software maintenance contracts did not have to be renewed, resulting in a $0.2 million reduction in expense. &#160;The remaining $0.3&#160;million in reduced expenses was related to labor and labor-related expenses, telephony costs and other office expenses, consistent with the reduction in contracts to service.</div>

<div style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 9pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(9.7</div>
</td>
<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: left; WIDTH: 1%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" valign="bottom" nowrap="nowrap">
<div style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 9pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">)%</div>
</td>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Payment Solutions General and Administrative:</u></font> &#160;Several factors contributed to the overall decrease in G&amp;A expenses during fiscal 2011. &#160;Share-based payment expense decreased $1.3&#160;million when comparing fiscal 2011 to 2010. &#160;During fiscal 2011, we reversed $1.5&#160;million in share-based payment expense related to Restricted Stock Units, (RSUs) granted to a former CEO. &#160;RSU vesting conditions were not satisfied and we reversed the expense that had been previously recognized. &#160;Two factors contributed to a $0.2&#160;million increase to share-based payment expense in fiscal 2011: (1) we granted every employee options to purchase shares of our stock, which led to an increase in the total number of shares vesting and the associated expense, and (2) fiscal 2010 benefitted from significant credits to share-based payment expense due to our Performance Stock Units, (PSUs), as well as a declining stock price.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal 2010 we recorded nearly $1.5&#160;million in severance expense related to the departure of a former CEO and former COO. &#160;During fiscal 2011, we recorded approximately $0.5&#160;million in severance expense related to the departure of our former CFO and the severance expense related to the transition of our corporate office to Norcross, Georgia. &#160;This resulted in a $1.0&#160;million net expense reduction in fiscal 2011 over the prior year. &#160;Fiscal 2011 management incentive plan expense was $0.8&#160;million less than in fiscal 2010 because we did not meet our fiscal 2011 performance goals.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; FONT-SIZE: 9pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">24</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our legal expenses decreased $0.9&#160;million in fiscal 2011 versus fiscal 2010, primarily due to one-time legal costs incurred during fiscal 2010 related to corporate governance matters and our annual meeting and proxy statement. &#160;Our facilities related costs decreased $0.6&#160;million in fiscal 2011 over fiscal 2010 due to a full year benefit of reduced rent expense for our Reston office as well as the absence of restructuring costs related to our San Ramon, California, Tulsa, Oklahoma and Auburn, Alabama office consolidations. &#160;During fiscal 2011 we increased our collection efforts on accounts receivable and as a result we re-evaluated our estimate for bad debts which resulted in a $0.5&#160;million decrease in bad debt expense in fiscal 2011 versus fiscal 2010.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Further contributing to the overall reduction in G&amp;A expenses in fiscal 2011 versus fiscal 2010 were: a $0.4&#160;million reduction in telephony costs as a result of reduced pricing agreements placed into effect late in fiscal 2010; a $0.2&#160;million reduction in recruiting expense as a result of expenses incurred in fiscal 2010 for our CEO search; and $0.1&#160;million in reduced travel and travel-related expenses.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Primarily offsetting these decreases was an increase in labor and labor-related costs of $2.3&#160;million in fiscal 2011 versus fiscal 2010, a result of additional positions added at the senior executive level, the addition of software developers, a decrease in internally developed software projects that capitalize labor, and an increase in maintenance work on existing platforms. &#160;In addition, our outside consultant and services labor costs increased $0.7&#160;million in fiscal 2011 versus fiscal 2010. &#160;Our software and equipment purchases and maintenance agreements increased $0.4&#160;million in fiscal 2011 versus fiscal 2010, consistent with previously discussed network upgrade initiatives. &#160;Finally, our money transmitter license and fee expense increased $0.3&#160;million primarily attributable to obtaining licenses in several new states.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>VSA General and Administrative:</u></font> &#160;The decrease in fiscal 2011 for VSA G&amp;A expenses relates primarily to an adjustment to bad debt expense in fiscal 2011 relating to a Pension contract payment received that had been fully reserved.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Selling and Marketing (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

Our sales commission expense increased $0.1&#160;million year-over-year, as a result of the structure of our fiscal 2011 commission plan. &#160;Offsetting these increases is a decrease in marketing research of $0.2&#160;million and a $0.1&#160;million decrease in labor and labor-related expenses, including consultants and outside services.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2010 we placed several internally developed software projects into service with a three year useful life, resulting in a full year of depreciation expense recorded during fiscal 2011. &#160;This was the primary reason for the increase in depreciation and amortization expense for Payment Solutions. &#160;We did not incur any depreciation or amortization expense for our VSA operation during fiscal 2011, consistent with our plan to wind down the VSA business.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Other Income (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Interest income, net: </u></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>Fiscal 2011 interest income decreased $0.3&#160;million compared to fiscal 2010, attributable to both a decrease in the size of our investment portfolio and decreases in interest rates. &#160;Due to current market conditions, we elected to sell the municipal bonds we then owned and invest the proceeds in money market accounts, treasury bills, discount notes and commercial paper &#8211; often at lower interest rates than were being paid by the municipal bonds.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Income Tax Provision (Continuing Operations)</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We reported an income tax benefit from continuing operations of $100,000 for fiscal 2011, as compared to &#160; fiscal 2010, in which we recorded a provision of $30,000. The provision for income taxes represents state tax obligations incurred by our Payment Solutions operations and an intra-period tax allocation between continuing and discontinued operations. &#160;Our Consolidated Statements of Operations for fiscal 2011 and 2010 do not reflect a federal tax provision because of offsetting adjustments to our deferred tax asset valuation allowance.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL RESOURCES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At September&#160;30, 2012 we had $39.1&#160;million in cash and cash equivalents compared with $39.8&#160;million at September&#160;30, 2011. &#160;The decline in cash and cash equivalents is primarily associated with the acquisition of network-related infrastructure and spending on internally developed software.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As discussed in </font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Note 5&#8212;Customer Concentration and Risk</font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> and </font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Note 9&#8212;Commitments and Contingencies</font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> our Consolidated Balance Sheets include settlements receivable and payable. &#160;We had $39.1&#160;million in cash and cash equivalents at September 30, 2012. &#160;We had $15.3 million of settlements receivable at September 30, 2012 which we collected within two days of the fiscal year end as settlements from credit card companies and banks. We had $17.0 million of settlements payable and $5.6 million of accrued discount fees as of September 30, 2012 that we had not yet distributed to clients due to the timing of bank transactions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July 2011 we committed $8.3&#160;million to upgrade our infrastructure, which included the purchase of hardware, software and professional services. &#160;The project commenced in August 2011 and was completed and put into service in September 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We believe we have sufficient liquidity to meet currently anticipated needs, including capital expenditures, working capital investments, and acquisitions for the next twelve months. &#160;We expect to generate cash flows from operating activities over the long term; however, we may experience significant fluctuations from quarter to quarter as a result of the timing of billing and collections, and the related settlement of funds. &#160;To the extent that our existing capital resources are insufficient to meet our capital requirements, we would have to raise additional funds. &#160;There can be no assurance that such additional funding, if necessary, would be available on favorable terms, if at all. &#160;Currently, we do not have any short or long-term debt.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations is based on our Consolidated Financial Statements, which have been prepared in accordance with US GAAP. &#160;Note 2&#8212;Summary of Significant Accounting and Reporting Policies of our Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements contains a summary of our significant accounting policies, many of which require the use of estimates and assumptions. &#160;We believe that of our significant policies, the following are the most noteworthy because they are based upon estimates and assumptions that require complex subjective judgments by management, which can have a material effect on our reported results. &#160;Changes in these estimates or assumptions could materially affect our financial condition and results of operations. &#160;Actual results could differ materially from management's estimates.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Revenue Recognition</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Electronic payment processing revenue:</font> Electronic payment processing and fee income is derived from the electronic processing of credit and debit card transactions that are captured and authorized through third-party networks. We charge a convenience fee for these processing services which is either a percentage of the dollar amount of each transaction or a flat fee per transaction. Certain Clients are charged miscellaneous fees, including fees for handling charge-backs or returns, monthly minimum fees, statement fees and fees for other miscellaneous services. Revenues derived from the electronic processing of credit and debit card transactions are reported gross of amounts paid to sponsor banks in the form of discount fees. We recognize the revenue in the month in which the service is provided.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">VSA revenue:</font> VSA revenue is primarily derived from annual recurring service fees for the use of the service and related support services. Customer set-up fees are billed upon service initiation and are recognized as revenue over the estimated customer relationship period of 2.5 years. Payment for VSA and related services is generally received one month to one year in advance. Deferred revenues are recognized for customer payments for services in advance of the performance of services for the customer.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Goodwill and Intangible Assets</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Acquired goodwill and intangible assets are initially recorded at fair value and tested for impairment at least annually or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of goodwill may not be recoverable. All of our goodwill and intangible assets are included in our Payment Solutions reporting unit.&#160;Goodwill is evaluated for possible impairment by comparing the fair value of a</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">reporting unit with its carrying value, including the goodwill assigned to that reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Fair value of the reporting unit is estimated using a combination of income-based and market-based valuation methodologies. &#160;Under the income approach, forecasted cash flows of a reporting unit are discounted to a present value using a discount rate commensurate with the risks of those cash flows. &#160;Under the market approach, the fair value of a reporting unit is estimated based on trading multiples of a group of comparable public companies and from values implied by recent merger and acquisition transactions involving comparable companies. &#160;An impairment charge is recorded if the carrying value of the Payment Solutions reporting unit exceeds its implied fair value. &#160;We performed our annual impairment test of the carrying value of our goodwill for fiscal 2012 during our fourth quarter; this is consistent with the historic timing of our annual goodwill impairment review. Based on our assessment as of September 30, 2012, we concluded that the fair value of the Payment Solutions reporting unit exceeded its carrying value by at least 50%.&#160;&#160;Significant assumptions inherent in the valuation methodologies employed include, but are not limited to, projected business results, growth rates and discount rates.&#160;&#160;These assumptions are based primarily on our historical results and expectations for future operations.&#160;&#160;Our assumptions do not include the potential impacts of alternative payment methods Customers might begin to use, significant changes in the overall economy or loss of significant Clients, each of which would likely decrease our estimated fair value and potentially cause us to record an impairment of our recorded goodwill.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At September 30, 2012, the carrying value of goodwill was approximately $17.6 million.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to our annual goodwill impairment review, we also perform periodic reviews of the carrying values of our other intangible assets. These intangible assets consist primarily of acquired core technology and acquired customer related assets. In evaluating potential impairment of these assets we specifically consider whether any indicators of impairment are present, including:</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If indicators of impairment are present, an estimate of the undiscounted cash flows that the specific asset is expected to generate must be made to ensure that the carrying value of the asset can be recovered. These estimates involve significant subjectivity. At September 30, 2012, the carrying value of our intangible assets, excluding goodwill, was approximately $1.1 million. As a result of our fiscal 2012 impairment review, we concluded that none of these assets was impaired.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Income Taxes</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We account for income taxes by recognizing deferred tax assets and liabilities, which are recorded to reflect the future tax consequences attributable to the effects of differences between the carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities for financial reporting and for income tax purposes. Judgments are required in determining the amount and probability of future taxable income, which in turn is critical to a determination of whether a valuation reserve against the deferred tax asset is appropriate.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We also account for the recognition and measurement of tax benefits associated with uncertain tax positions. This requires evaluations of individual tax positions to determine whether any part of that position can be recognized or continue to be recognized in the financial statements. An uncertain tax position exists if it is unclear how a transaction will be treated under tax law. As of September&#160;30, 2012 and 2011, we had no unrecognized tax benefits.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><u>Share-Based Compensation</u></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the provisions of ASC 718, share-based compensation cost for stock option awards is estimated at the grant date based on the award's fair value as calculated by the Black-Scholes option-pricing formula and is recognized as expense ratably over the requisite service period. We recognize share -based</div>
