<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">compensation costs for only those shares that are expected to vest. The impact of forfeitures that may occur prior to vesting is estimated and considered in the amount of expense recognized. Forfeiture estimates are revised in subsequent periods when actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. The Black-Scholes option-pricing formula requires various highly judgmental assumptions including volatility and expected option life. If any of the assumptions used in the Black-Scholes model change significantly, share-based compensation expense may differ materially for future awards from that recorded for existing awards.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">RECENT ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>FASB ASU 2011-04</u></font>. &#160;In May 2011, the FASB issued FASB ASU 2011-04, which clarifies some existing concepts, eliminates wording differences between US GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards, or IFRS, and changes some of the principles and disclosures of fair value measurement to achieve convergence between US GAAP and IFRS. &#160;ASU 2011-04 also expands the disclosures for fair value measurements that are estimated using significant unobservable (Level 3) inputs. &#160;We adopted this ASU effective January&#160;1, 2012. &#160;The initial adoption of this ASU did not have a material impact on our financial position or results of operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>FASB ASU 2011-08</u></font>. &#160;In September 2011, the FASB issued FASB ASU 2011-08, which allows entities testing for impairment of goodwill the option of performing a qualitative assessment before calculating the fair value of a reporting unit in step 1 of the goodwill impairment test. &#160;If, after assessing the totality of events or circumstances, an entity determines it is more likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit is more than its carrying amount, then performing the two-step impairment test is unnecessary. However, if an entity concludes otherwise, then it is required to perform the first step of the two-step impairment test. &#160;We will adopt this ASU effective October 1, 2012. &#160;We do not believe the adoption of this ASU will have a material impact on our financial position or results of operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>FASB ASU 2011-11</u></font>. &#160;In December 2011, the FASB issued FASB ASU 2011-11, which requires entities to disclose information about offsetting and related arrangements to enable users of financial statements to understand the effect of those arrangements on an entity's financial position. The amendments require enhanced disclosures about financial instruments and derivative instruments that are either (i) offset in accordance with current literature or (ii) subject to an enforceable master netting arrangement or similar agreement, irrespective of whether they are offset in accordance with current literature. ASU 2011-11 is effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2013. This standard will become effective for us beginning October 2013. The disclosures required by ASU 2011-11 will be applied retrospectively for all comparative periods presented. We are currently evaluating the impact of ASU 2011-11.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>FASB ASU 2012-02.</u></font> &#160;In July 2012 the FASB issued FASB ASU 2012-02 regarding the testing of indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment. &#160;An entity will have an option not to calculate annually the fair value of an indefinite-lived intangible asset if the entity determines that it is not more likely than not that the asset is impaired. &#160;This standard permits an entity to assess qualitative factors when testing indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment results in guidance that is similar to the goodwill impairment testing guidance. &#160;This is effective <font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">for annual and interim impairment tests performed for fiscal years beginning after September 15, 2012. We do not believe the adoption of this standard will have any impact on our financial statements or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our Certificate of Incorporation obligates us to indemnify our directors and officers against all expenses, judgments, fines and amounts paid in settlement for which such persons become liable as a result of acting in any capacity on behalf of Official Payments, if the director or officer met the standard of conduct specified in the Certificate, and subject to the limitations specified in the Certificate. &#160;In addition, we have indemnification agreements with certain of our directors and officers, which supplement the indemnification obligations in our Certificate. &#160;These agreements generally obligate us to indemnify the indemnitees' against expenses incurred because of their status as a director or officer, if the indemnitee met the standard of conduct specified in the agreement, and subject to the limitations specified in the agreement.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Arial Bold', serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 2&#8212;SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING AND REPORTING POLICIES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Basis of Presentation.</u></font> &#160;These financial statements and the accompanying notes are prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, and conform to Regulation S-X under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Principles of Consolidation.</u></font> &#160;The financial statements include the accounts of Official Payments Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiary. &#160;Intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Use of Estimates.</u></font> &#160;Preparing financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported on our Consolidated Financial Statements and accompanying notes. &#160;We believe that near-term changes could reasonably affect the following estimates: &#160;collectability of receivables; share-based compensation; valuation of goodwill, intangibles and investments; contingent liabilities; effective tax rates; and deferred taxes and the associated valuation allowance. &#160;Although we believe the estimates and assumptions used in preparing our Consolidated Financial Statements and notes thereto are reasonable in light of known facts and circumstances, actual results could differ materially.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Cash and Cash Equivalents.</u></font> &#160;Cash is federally insured funds maintained in demand deposit accounts. &#160;Cash equivalents are highly liquid investments with maturities of three months or less at the date of purchase and are stated at amounts that approximate fair value, based on quoted market prices. &#160;Cash equivalents consist principally of investments in interest-bearing demand deposit accounts with financial institutions and U.S. Treasury bills.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Revenue Recognition and Credit Risk.</u></font> &#160;Payment Solutions revenues are primarily attributable to fees for processing incoming payment obligations electronically. &#160;We recognize revenue when persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, delivery has occurred, the fee is fixed or determinable, and collectability is</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; FONT-SIZE: 9pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">40</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Back to table of contents<br>
</a></div>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">reasonably assured. &#160;We assess collectability based upon our Clients' financial condition and prior payment history, as well as our performance under the arrangement.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our Payment Solutions operations offer services that allow our Clients to offer their Constituents (individuals or businesses) the ability to pay certain financial obligations with credit or debit cards, electronic check, cash or money order, depending on the terms of the arrangement. &#160;Our revenue is generated in the form of the convenience fee we are permitted to charge for the electronic payment solutions service provided. &#160;Depending on the agreement with the Client, the convenience fee can be a fixed fee or a percentage of the payment processed. &#160;In over 90% of our arrangements, this fee is charged directly to the Constituent and is added to their payment obligation when it is processed. &#160;In the remainder of arrangements, our Clients pay the convenience fees we receive. &#160;We recognize the revenue in the month in which the service is provided.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal 2012, our VSA operations included software maintenance and support and non-essential training and consulting support. &#160;When we provide ongoing maintenance and support services, the associated revenue is deferred and recognized on a straight-line basis over the life of the related contract&#8212;typically one year. &#160;Generally, we recognize the revenues earned for non-essential training and consulting support when the services are performed.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Allowance for Doubtful Accounts.</u></font> &#160;The allowance for doubtful accounts reflects our best estimate of probable losses inherent in the accounts receivable balance. &#160;We determine the allowance for doubtful accounts based on known troubled accounts, historical experience and other currently available evidence. &#160;Additions to the allowance for doubtful accounts are included in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General and administrative</font> on our Consolidated Statements of Operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Settlements receivable.</u></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font> Individuals and businesses settle their obligations to our various Clients, primarily utility and other public sector Clients, using credit or debit cards or via ACH payments. &#160;We create a receivable for the amount due from the credit or debit card company or bank and an offsetting payable to the Client. &#160;Once we receive confirmation the funds have been received, we settle the obligation to the Client. &#160;Convenience fees are charged to cardholders on a per transaction basis and are reinstated to cardholders upon an approved payment reversal.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Accrued Discount Fees.</u></font> &#160;Our direct costs for our Payment Solutions operations primarily consist of credit card discount fees, in addition to assessments and other costs passed onto us by our processors. &#160;Collectively, these fees and costs are considered to be discount fees. &#160;Discount fees are charged to us as a percentage of the dollar volume we transact plus a fixed fee, and for expense purposes, are incurred during the month that the related transaction is authorized for payment. &#160;Accrued discount fees represent the total amount of discount fees that have been incurred by us on authorized transactions, but have yet to be remitted by us as of the reporting date. &#160;Discount fees are typically remitted by us in the calendar month which follows the date of transaction authorization.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Fair Value of Financial Instruments.</u></font> &#160;The carrying amounts of certain financial instruments, including cash equivalents, restricted cash, accounts receivable, accounts payable and accrued liabilities, approximate fair value due to their short maturities.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Advertising Expense.</u></font> &#160;We expense advertising costs, net of cooperative advertising cash contributions received from partners, during the period the advertising takes place. &#160;We incurred net advertising expenses from Continuing Operations of $1.6&#160;million during fiscal 2012, $1.3&#160;million during fiscal year 2011, and $0.7&#160;million during fiscal year 2010.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Property, Equipment and Software.</u></font> &#160;Property, equipment and software are stated at cost and depreciated using the straight-line method over the shorter of the estimated useful lives of the assets or the lease terms, ranging from two to seven years. &#160;When assets are retired or otherwise disposed of, the cost and accumulated depreciation are removed from the accounts and any resulting gain or loss is reflected in operations in the period realized.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We expense the costs incurred for software that we expect to use internally until the preliminary project stage has been completed. &#160;Subsequently, we capitalize direct service and material costs, as well as direct payroll</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; FONT-SIZE: 9pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">41</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Back to table of contents<br>
</a></div>
</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">and payroll&#8209;related costs and interest costs incurred during development. &#160;Once the software is ready for its intended use in accordance with ASC 350-40, we amortize it on a straight-line basis over its estimated useful life.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Goodwill</u></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>.</u></font> &#160;Goodwill is not amortized, but instead is tested for impairment at least annually at the reporting unit level. &#160;We perform this impairment test by first comparing the fair value of our Payment Solutions reporting units to their carrying amount. &#160;If an indicator of impairment exists, we would then compare the implied fair value of our goodwill to the carrying amount in order to determine the amount of the impairment, if any. &#160;We determine fair value of our reporting units using various methodologies including: 1) comparable public companies; 2) merger and acquisitions precedents; and 3) discounted cash flows &#160;No impairment existed during fiscal 2012. </div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Intangible Assets.</u></font> &#160;We amortize intangible assets with finite lives over their estimated benefit period, ranging from five to ten years, in a manner consistent with the estimated pattern in which the asset is consumed. &#160;We evaluate the recoverability of intangible assets periodically and take into account events or circumstances that warrant revised estimates of useful lives or that indicate that impairment exists. &#160;No impairment existed during fiscal 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Loss Per Share.</u></font> &#160;Basic loss per share is computed by dividing net loss by the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding for the period. &#160;Diluted earnings per share reflect the potential dilution that could occur if securities or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock to the extent such securities or other contracts are not anti-dilutive.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Share-Based Compensation.</u></font> &#160;Share-based compensation cost for an option award is measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized as expense over the applicable vesting period of the award (typically three to five years) using the ratable method. &#160;We also issue restricted stock units and performance stock units. &#160;For the restricted stock units and performance stock units payable in cash, we record expense based on the fair value of the awards at the end of each financial reporting period, consistent with the recognition of awards classified as liabilities under US GAAP.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Income Taxes.</u></font> &#160;Deferred income taxes are provided for the tax effect of temporary differences between the tax basis of assets and liabilities and their reported amounts in the financial statements. &#160;The liability method is used to account for income taxes, which requires deferred taxes to be recorded at the statutory rate expected to be in effect when the taxes are paid or the differences are reversed. &#160;Valuation allowances are established against net deferred tax assets when it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. &#160;We recognize the tax benefit or liability of an uncertain tax position only if it is more-likely-than-not that the tax position will be sustained on examination by the taxing authorities, based on the technical merits of the position.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Accumulated Comprehensive (Loss) Income.</u></font> &#160;Our accumulated comprehensive (loss) income is composed of net (loss) income and unrealized (losses) gains on marketable investment securities, net of related taxes.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">RECENT ACCOUNTING PRONOUNCEMENTS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>FASB ASU 2011-04</u></font>. &#160;In May 2011, the FASB issued FASB ASU 2011-04, which clarifies some existing concepts, eliminates wording differences between US GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards, or IFRS, and changes some of the principles and disclosures of fair value measurement to achieve convergence between US GAAP and IFRS. &#160;ASU 2011-04 also expands the disclosures for fair value measurements that are estimated using significant unobservable (Level 3) inputs. &#160;We adopted this ASU effective January&#160;1, 2012. &#160;The initial adoption of this ASU did not have a material impact on our financial position or results of operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>FASB ASU 2011-08</u></font>. &#160;In September 2011, the FASB issued FASB ASU 2011-08, which allows entities testing for impairment of goodwill the option of performing a qualitative assessment before calculating the fair value of a reporting unit in step 1 of the goodwill impairment test. &#160;If, after assessing the totality of events or circumstances, an entity determines it is more likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit is more than its</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; FONT-SIZE: 9pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">42</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Back to table of contents<br>
</a></div>
</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">carrying amount, then performing the two-step impairment test is unnecessary. However, if an entity concludes otherwise, then it is required to perform the first step of the two-step impairment test. &#160;We will adopt this ASU effective October 1, 2012. &#160;We do not believe the adoption of this ASU will have a material impact on our financial position or results of operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>FASB ASU 2011-11</u></font>. &#160;In December 2011, the FASB issued FASB ASU 2011-11, which requires entities to disclose information about offsetting and related arrangements to enable users of financial statements to understand the effect of those arrangements on an entity's financial position. The amendments require enhanced disclosures about financial instruments and derivative instruments that are either (i) offset in accordance with current literature or (ii) subject to an enforceable master netting arrangement or similar agreement, irrespective of whether they are offset in accordance with current literature. ASU 2011-11 is effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2013. This standard will become effective for us beginning October 2013. The disclosures required by ASU 2011-11 will be applied retrospectively for all comparative periods presented. We are currently evaluating the impact of ASU 2011-11.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>FASB ASU 2012-02.</u></font> &#160;In July 2012 the FASB issued FASB ASU 2012-02 regarding the testing of indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment. &#160;An entity will have an option not to calculate annually the fair value of an indefinite-lived intangible asset if the entity determines that it is not more likely than not that the asset is impaired. &#160;Permitting an entity to assess qualitative factors when testing indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment results in guidance that is similar to the goodwill impairment testing guidance. &#160;This is effective <font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">for annual and interim impairment tests performed for fiscal years beginning after September 15, 2012. We do not believe the adoption of this standard will have any impact on our financial statements or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 3&#8212;INVESTMENTS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At September&#160;30, 2012 all of our investments are classified as cash equivalents and are included in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font> on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. &#160;Unrestricted investments with original maturities of 90 days or less (as of the date that we purchased the securities) are classified as cash equivalents.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 4&#8212;FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Fair value is defined under US GAAP as the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date. &#160;Valuation techniques used to measure fair value must maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs. &#160;The fair value hierarchy is based on three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair value as follows:</div>

<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: Arial; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 11.71%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 1&#8212;</div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 88.29%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</div>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 11.71%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 2&#8212;</div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 88.29%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Inputs other than quoted prices in active markets, that are observable, either directly or indirectly, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities.</div>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 11.71%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 3&#8212;</div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 88.29%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Unobservable inputs, for which there is little or no market data for the assets or liabilities.</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Accounts receivable, net.</u></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font> As of September&#160;30, 2012 and 2011, we reported $5.3&#160;million and $4.5&#160;million, respectively, in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accounts receivable, net </font>on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. &#160;This item represents receivables from our Clients that we expect to receive, offset by an allowance for doubtful accounts. &#160;Approximately 3.0% and 7.0% of the balances reported at September 30, 2012 and 2011, respectively, represent accounts receivable attributable to operations that we intend to wind down during fiscal 2013 and fiscal 2014. &#160;The remainder of the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accounts receivable, net</font> balance is composed of receivables from certain of our Payment Solutions Clients. &#160;None of our Payment Solutions Clients have receivables that exceed 10% of our total receivable balance. &#160;As of September&#160;30, 2012 and 2011, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accounts receivable, net</font> included an allowance for doubtful accounts of $0.2&#160;million and $0.4&#160;million, respectively, representing the balance of receivables for which we believe collectability is not reasonably assured.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Settlements receivable.</u></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font> As of September&#160;30, 2012 and 2011, we reported $15.3&#160;million and $7.6&#160;million in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Settlements receivable </font>on our Consolidated Balance Sheets, which represents amounts due from credit or debit card companies or banks. &#160;Individuals and businesses settle their obligations to our various Clients, using credit or debit cards or via ACH payments. &#160;We record a receivable for the amount due from the credit or debit card company or bank and an offsetting payable to the Client. &#160;Once we receive confirmation the funds have been received, we settle the obligation to the Client. &#160;See Note 9&#8212;Commitments and Contingencies for information about the settlements payable to our Clients.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 7&#8212;GOODWILL AND OTHER INTANGIBLE ASSETS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">GOODWILL</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">As a result of our acquisition of substantially all of the assets of ChoicePay, Inc. in January 2009, we may be required to pay up to $2.0&#160;million through December&#160;31, 2013, based on a percentage of the gross profits generated by specific Client contracts. &#160;Any payment is recorded as additional goodwill associated with the asset acquisition. &#160;As of September 30, 2012, we have paid ChoicePay approximately $285,000. We expect the potential payments will not exceed $200,000 over the remaining life of the agreement. &#160;The following table summarizes changes in the carrying amount of goodwill during fiscal 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We test goodwill for impairment during the fourth quarter of each fiscal year at the reporting unit level using a fair value approach. &#160;If an event occurs or circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying value, we would evaluate goodwill for impairment between annual tests. &#160;No such event occurred during fiscal year 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when, in the opinion of management, it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. &#160;In evaluating our ability to realize deferred tax assets, we considered all available positive and negative evidence. &#160;As of September&#160;30, 2012, we maintained a full valuation allowance against the net deferred tax assets due to the uncertainty regarding utilization. &#160;As of September&#160;30, 2012, a total of $20.0&#160;million of the valuation allowance related to deferred tax assets for which any subsequently recognized tax benefits would be subject to FASB ASC&#160;805. &#160;Therefore adjustments to the valuation allowances will be recorded as a component of income tax expense, and $2.6&#160;million of the valuation allowance related to deferred tax assets for which any subsequent recognized tax benefits would increase common stock.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have completed a detailed study regarding the application of Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (Section 382) which imposes an annual limitation on the utilization of net operating loss carryforwards following an ownership change. &#160;Application of the findings of this study resulted in a limitation of net operating loss carryforward amounts. &#160;Of the $125.7&#160;million of federal net operating loss carryforward and $109.0&#160;million on the state net operating loss carryforward, $48.6&#160;million and $28.1&#160;million, respectively, were acquired with the purchase of Official Payments Corporation in 2002 and have restrictions.&#160; As of September&#160;30, 2012 approximately $108.3 million of our federal net operating loss carryforwards do not have any restrictions.&#160; Our acquired federal net operating loss carryforward is limited to $3.4 million per year pursuant to Internal Revenue Code Section 382, and approximately $11.2&#160;million is still limited to this annual amount.&#160; If future ownership changes occur, there could be further limitations to our federal net operating loss carryforwards.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of September&#160;30, 2012 there is an AMT tax credit carryover of $38,000 and a Research and Development tax credit carryover of $18,000. &#160;The AMT tax credit has no expiration date and the Research and Development tax credit begins to expire in 2025. &#160;Both credit carryovers have a valuation allowance associated with them, as it is deemed more likely than not that these credits will not be realized in the future.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Generally, the amount of tax expense or benefit allocated to continuing operations is determined without regard to the tax effects of other categories of income or loss, such as discontinued operations, extraordinary items, other comprehensive income and items charged or credited to shareholders' equity. &#160;However, an exception to the general rule is provided when there is a pre-tax loss from continuing operations and pre-tax income from other categories in the current year. &#160;In such instances, income from other categories must be considered in allocating the aggregate tax provision for the period among the various categories. &#160;The intra-period tax allocation rules in ASC 740-20 related to items charged directly to other categories of income or loss can result in deferred tax assets or liabilities that remain until certain events occur. &#160;Income tax benefit related to Continuing Operations for fiscal year ended September&#160;30, 2011 includes a benefit of nearly $124,000 due to the required intra-period tax allocation. &#160;Conversely, Discontinued Operations for fiscal 2011 includes a charge of nearly $124,000 related to a gain on disposal of discontinued operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UNRECOGNIZED TAX BENEFITS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have examined our current and past tax positions taken, and have concluded that it is more likely than not these tax positions will be sustained in the event of an examination and that there would be no material impact to our effective tax rate. &#160;In the event interest or penalties had been accrued, our policy is to include these amounts related to unrecognized tax benefits in income tax expense. &#160;As of September&#160;30, 2012 we had no accrued interest or penalties related to uncertain tax positions. &#160;We file tax returns with the IRS and in various states in which the statute of limitations may go back to the tax year ended September&#160;30, 2008. &#160;As of September&#160;30, 2012, we were not engaged in a federal income tax audit. Currently, we are in the process of providing information for a Virginia state income tax audit covering November 1, 2007 through October 31, 2010.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of September&#160;30, 2012 and 2011, we had no unrecognized tax benefits.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Arial Bold', serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 9&#8212;COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">LEGAL ISSUES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">From time to time during the normal course of business, we are a party to litigation and/or other claims. &#160;At September&#160;30, 2012, none of these matters was expected to have a material impact on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows. &#160;At September&#160;30, 2012 and September&#160;30, 2011, we had legal accruals of $0.5&#160;million and $0.8&#160;million, respectively, based upon estimates of key legal matters.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SETTLEMENTS PAYABLE</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Settlements payable</font> on our Consolidated Balance Sheets consists of payments due primarily to utilities, higher education, and public sector Clients. &#160;As individuals and businesses settle their obligations to our various Clients, we generate a receivable from the credit or debit card company and a payable to the Client. &#160;Once we receive confirmation the funds have been received by the card company, we settle the liabilities to the Client. &#160;This process may take several business days to complete and can result in unsettled funds at the end of a reporting period. &#160;We had $17.0&#160;million and $9.8&#160;million, respectively, of settlements payable at September 30,&#160;2012 and September&#160;30, 2011.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CREDIT RISK</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We maintain our cash and cash equivalents in bank deposit accounts and money market accounts. &#160;Typically, the balance in a number of these accounts significantly exceeds federally insured limits. &#160;We have not experienced any losses in such accounts and believe that any associated credit risk is <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">de minimis</font>. &#160;At September&#160;30, 2012, our investment portfolio is composed of money market funds. &#160;The reported value of our investment portfolio and cash and cash equivalents approximates fair value.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">PERFORMANCE, BID AND GUARANTEE PAYMENT BONDS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the terms of money transmitter licenses we hold with individual states, we are required to provide guarantee payment bonds from a licensed surety. &#160;At September 30, 2012, we had $12.9&#160;million of bonds posted in connection with state money transmitter licenses. &#160;There were no claims pending against any of these bonds.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under certain contracts or bids, we are required to obtain performance or bid bonds from a licensed surety and to post the performance bonds with our customers. &#160;Fees for obtaining the bonds are expensed over the life of each bond. &#160;At September 30, 2012, we had $4.1&#160;million of bonds posted with Clients. &#160;There were no claims pending against any of these bonds.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In February 2009, we completed the sale of our Unemployment Insurance, or UI, business as part of our divestment of several business units. &#160;Our sale of the UI business was completed pursuant to an Asset Purchase Agreement dated February&#160;6, 2009 and included the State of Indiana Unemployment Insurance contract as an asset. &#160;We retain certain contractual liabilities in connection with completion of the project, and we continue as the indemnitor under a $2.4 million performance bond on the continuing contract with the State of Indiana. Completion of the project has been delayed and additional funding has been required to continue the project. &#160;In 2009, as part of a contractually required mediation we offered a $420,000 contribution towards project completion; however the matter was not resolved. &#160;An additional mediation is expected to take place promptly after the project is finished, however there is no projected date for completion of the project. &#160;We anticipate the performance bond remaining in place until final resolution of the matter.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Amounts accrued for such contingencies are included in other accrued liabilities within our consolidated balance sheets.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENTS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of September&#160;30, 2012, we had employment and change of control agreements with several key employees. &#160;If certain termination or change of control events were to occur under these contracts as of September&#160;30, 2012, we could be required to pay up to $3.9&#160;million.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 10&#8212;RESTRUCTURING</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the quarter ended December 31, 2011, we moved our principal executive offices from Reston, Virginia to Norcross, Georgia to reduce general and administrative costs and take advantage of the electronic payments industry employee resources in the Atlanta area. &#160;We incurred total expenses of approximately $1.6&#160;million, including $0.1&#160;million of employee relocation cost and $1.5&#160;million of facilities related restructuring cost during the year ended September 30, 2012. &#160;We have vacated and sublet our Reston, Virginia facility as of December 31, 2011. &#160;In connection with vacating and subletting our Reston, Virginia facility in December 2011 we wrote off certain balances associated with our original lease agreement including net leasehold improvements of $1.0 million, and deferred rent. &#160;We also recorded an obligation for the remaining lease payments less sublease income. &#160;Our Reston, Virginia facility lease ends in April 2018. &#160;For fiscal 2012 we received $0.2 million in sublease payments. &#160;We expect to receive $3.1 million in future sublease payments over the remaining terms of the subleases. &#160;The restructuring charge is included in General and administrative expense in the accompanying Consolidated Statements of Operations and is within the Payment Solutions reporting segment.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 12&#8212;SHARE-BASED PAYMENT</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock options are issued under the Amended and Restated 2004 Stock Incentive Plan, or the Plan. &#160;The Plan provides our Board of Directors discretion in creating employee equity incentives, including incentive and non-statutory stock options. &#160;Options granted in and after August 2010 typically vest over four years, with 25% of the shares subject to each grant vesting on the first anniversary of the grant date and an additional 1/48<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">th</sup> of the shares vesting each month thereafter until the fourth anniversary of the grant date, and expire ten years from the grant date. &#160;Options granted prior to August 2010 typically vest over five years, with 20% of the shares subject to each grant vesting on each of the first five anniversaries of the grant date, and expire ten years from the grant date. &#160;At September&#160;30, 2012, there were 1,272,474 shares of common stock available for future issuance under the Plan.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">STOCK OPTIONS&#8212;AMENDED AND RESTATED 2004 STOCK INCENTIVE PLAN</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following table shows the weighted-average assumptions we used to calculate the fair value of share-based options using the Black-Scholes model, as well as the weighted-average fair value of options granted and the weighted-average intrinsic value of options exercised. &#160;We granted 482,250 options from the Plan during fiscal 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">STOCK OPTIONS&#8212;INDUCEMENT GRANTS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On August 16, 2010, we granted our current CEO the option to purchase 100,000 shares of common stock as an inducement grant outside of the Plan. &#160;These options vest as to 25% of the original number of shares on the first anniversary of the grant date and as to an additional 1/48<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">th</sup> of the original number of shares on the same date in each succeeding month following the first anniversary of the grant date until the fourth anniversary of the grant date and expire ten years from the grant date.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June&#160;13, 2011, we granted our current CFO the option to purchase 250,000 shares of common stock as an inducement grant outside of the Plan. &#160;These options vest as to 25% of the original number of shares on the first anniversary of the grant date and as to an additional 1/48<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">th</sup> of the original number of shares on the same date in each succeeding month following the first anniversary of the grant date until the fourth anniversary of the grant date and expire ten years from the grant date.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock-based compensation expense for all stock-based compensation awards granted was based on the grant-date fair value using the Black-Scholes model. &#160;We recognize compensation expense for stock option awards on a ratable basis over the requisite service period of the award. &#160;Stock option based compensation expense was $1.4&#160;million for fiscal 2012, $1.0&#160;million for fiscal 2011 and $0.9&#160;million for fiscal 2010.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of September&#160;30, 2012 a total of $2.4&#160;million of unrecognized compensation cost related to stock options, net of estimated forfeitures, was expected to be recognized over a 2.55 year weighted-average period.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 13&#8212;SHAREHOLDERS' EQUITY</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of September 30, 2012, a total of 44,259,762 shares of $0.01 par value common stock were authorized, of which 16,641,621 shares were outstanding, and a total of 4,579,047 shares of preferred stock were authorized, of which none were outstanding. &#160;We did not declare any dividends during fiscal year ended September&#160;30, 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">COMMON STOCK REPURCHASE PROGRAM</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of our common stock in the open market in January 2009 and October 2003. &#160;Under these plans we repurchased 2,536,298 shares of our common stock for $21.0&#160;million. The shares are recorded as <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Treasury stock</font> on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. &#160;The authority to make purchases under these plans has terminated.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">TENDER OFFER</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December&#160;17, 2010, we commenced a tender offer to purchase up to $10.0&#160;million of our common stock within a price range of $5.80 per share to $6.20 per share.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the tender offer, we accepted for payment on January 20, 2011, and repurchased 1,639,344 shares of our common stock for a price of $6.10 per share, for a total cost of approximately $10.0&#160;million, excluding fees and expenses related to the offer. &#160;We have recorded the cost of this transaction as <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Treasury stock</font> on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">EQUITY INCENTIVE PLANS AND INDUCEMENT GRANTS</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under our Amended and Restated 2004 Stock Incentive Plan, options for 2,666,232 shares of common stock were outstanding at September&#160;30, 2012. &#160;A further 143,500 options for shares of common stock were outstanding under plans which existed prior to the Amended and Restated Stock 2004 Incentive Plan, and 350,000 options for shares of common stock were outstanding under executive inducement grants.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="ITEM9CHANGESINANDDISAGREE"><!--Anchor--></a>ITEM 9&#8212;CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">None.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="ITEM9ACONTROLSANDPROCEDUR"><!--Anchor--></a>ITEM 9A&#8212;CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">EVALUATION OF DISCLOSURE CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act) as of September 30, 2012. &#160;The term "disclosure controls and procedures" means controls and other procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by a company in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported, within the time periods specified in the SEC's rules and forms. &#160;Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to ensure that such information is accumulated and communicated to the company's management, including its principal executive and principal financial officers, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. &#160;Management recognizes that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving their objectives and management necessarily applies its judgment in evaluating the cost-benefit relationship of possible controls and procedures. &#160;Based on the evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures as of September 30, 2012, our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer concluded that as of that date, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MANAGEMENT'S REPORT ON INTERNAL CONTROL OVER FINANCIAL REPORTING</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting for the company. &#160;Internal control over financial reporting is defined in Rule 13a-15(f) or 15d-15(f) promulgated under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 as a process designed by, or under the supervision of, the company's principal executive and principal financial officers and effected by the company's board of directors, management and other personnel, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and includes those policies and procedures that:</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 3pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of September&#160;30, 2012. In making this assessment, our management used the criteria set forth by the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework</font>.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 3pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Based on our assessment, management concluded that, as of September&#160;30, 2012, our internal control over financial reporting is effective based on those criteria.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 3pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our independent auditors have issued an audit report on our internal control over financial reporting. &#160;This report appears on page .</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Board of Directors and Shareholders of Official Payments Holdings, Inc.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have audited Official Payments Holdings Inc. internal control over financial reporting as of September 30, 2012, based on criteria established in Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (the COSO criteria). Official Payments Holdings Inc. management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in the accompanying Management's Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our <font style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 11pt">audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a </font>material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company's internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. &#160;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In our opinion, Official Payments Holdings Inc. maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of September 30, 2012, based on the COSO criteria.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated balance sheet of Official Payments Holdings, Inc. as of September 30, 2012, and the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, shareholders' equity, and cash flows for the year then ended and our report dated December 14, 2012 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CHANGES IN INTERNAL CONTROL OVER FINANCIAL REPORTING</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There have been no changes in our internal control over financial reporting during the quarter ended September&#160;30, 2012 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="ITEM9BOTHERINFORMATION"><!--Anchor--></a>ITEM 9B&#8212;OTHER INFORMATION</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MANAGEMENT INCENTIVE PLAN FOR FISCAL 2013</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 10, 2012, the Compensation Committee (the "Committee") of the Company's Board of Directors adopted the Company's Management Incentive Plan for fiscal year 2013 and specified the range of potential payments under the plan. &#160;Alex P. Hart, President and Chief Executive Officer, Jeff Hodges, Chief Financial Officer, Sandip Mohapatra, Chief Technology Officer, Atul Garg, Senior Vice President, Corporate Development, Keith S. Omsberg, Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, and approximately 30 other Company employees are participants in the plan.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">
<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Payments under the plan will be based on the Company's financial performance and individual performance. &#160;The financial performance metric is Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations &#8211; defined as net income from continuing operations before interest expense net of interest income, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, restructuring charges and stock-based compensation in both equity and cash &#8211; subject to adjustments as may be determined by the Compensation Committee. &#160;The Committee specified threshold, target, and stretch levels of financial performance that will be used to determine payments under the plan. &#160;For the Company's executive officers, the Committee specified, on December 10, 2012, individual performance goals that relate to strategic objectives based on each such officer's area of responsibility; the Committee expects to establish, in the first quarter of calendar 2013, an additional individual performance goal related to strategic objectives. &#160;Individual performance goals for other participants in the plan will be set by the supervising manager and senior executive of the participant's business unit, and subject to Mr. Hart's review and approval, and are expected to reflect strategic goals based on the participant's business unit or area of responsibility.</div>

In order to align near-term incentives with the Company's financial performance, 80% of the payment under the plan to Alex P. Hart, Official Payments' President and CEO, will be based on the Company's financial performance, and 70% of the payment under the plan to Official Payments' other executive officers will be based on the Company's financial performance.&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN-TOP: 6pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Messrs. Hart, Hodges, Mohapatra, Garg, and Omsberg are participants in the plan. &#160;If the Company achieves the threshold, target, and stretch levels of financial performance, and if each of Messrs. Hart, Hodges, Mohapatra, Garg, and Omsberg achieves 100% of his individual performance goals, the following individuals would receive the following payments under the plan:</div>
